next_steps: Maya to share trimmed latency heatmap and cost delta by 2026-06-14
Liam to run failover dry-run on staging Tuesday and post logs
HelixPay to confirm success criteria for rollback (latency+error thresholds) by 2026-06-16
action_items: Maya Patel - produce per-route token-cost breakdown and share explainer (due 2026-06-14)
Liam O'Connor - execute staging rollback drill, capture traces and KV cache metrics (due 2026-06-16)

summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on model selection, version pinning mechanics, and a planned dry-run of fallback/rollback. Team validated tradeoffs between model latency and cost, agreed to run an automated rollback drill on staging, and to capture traces and cache warmup behavior. Security and data retention questions deferred to upcoming compliance packet review.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-11 14:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood), Jorge, Aisha, Lauren, Samir (HelixPay)
[00:00] Maya Patel: ok hi everyone thanks for joining on time, quick check — can we start with a 1 minute context recap, Jorge?
[00:10] Jorge Martinez: yeah sure, uh quick recap, we've been running the pilot for two weeks, primary flows are customer onboarding chat and reconciliation batch summarization. Latency target 350ms p95 on chat, cost target within 20% of current CPU baseline.
[00:25] Maya Patel: perfect. Today's focus is model selection + pinning: we want to do a dry-run of the rollback path to ensure cutover is safe. Liam, you wanna walk through the catalog diff?
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: yeah, I pulled three candidates from Redwood catalog — radix-v1 (high quality but heavier), radix-v1-q4 (quantized, cost win, slightly higher p95), and breeze-small (fast but weaker on long context). Important: the runtime supports soft-fallbacks so we can route by latency budget.
[00:50] Aisha Khan: can you clarify quantized tradeoffs — we saw hallucinations spike a bit in some summarization tests.
[01:00] Liam O'Connor: yup good call. quantization here reduces model FP precision, we saw a tiny bump in factuality in long summaries. but for chat short-context rhymes it was within acceptable gate. we flagged a prompt-set where it failed.
[01:15] Lauren Green: are we comfortable pinning radix-v1-q4 for production if we keep fallback to radix-v1? what's the rollback latency hit?
[01:25] Liam O'Connor: fallback to full radix-v1 means higher tokens ms and cost — p95 moves from ~280ms to ~430ms on our staging HW. that's why we want a soft-fence: allow routing to quantized by default, but automatically divert if p95 crosses 380ms for more than 2 minutes.
[01:45] Samir Desai: question on KV cache — when we swap models do we lose cache warmup and get a cold-cache penalty?
[01:52] Liam O'Connor: yes partially. different models have incompatible KV formats. Redwood runtime keeps cross-model cache only for compatible families; radix-v1-q4 and radix-v1 share architecture so warmup is fast, but backup models like breeze-small do not. We'll capture the measured warmup curve in the dry-run.
[02:10] Maya Patel: ok next, dry-run plan. Liam, can you outline the rollback drill steps?
[02:15] Liam O'Connor: step 1: run canary with 10% traffic to radix-v1-q4 for 30m, monitor latency/error and token cost. step 2: force a simulated degrade (throttle GPUs) to trigger the fallback policy. step 3: perform emergency swap to radix-v1 fully for 5m and observe client behavior. step 4: revert to q4 and monitor recovery. We'll collect traces, kv cache metrics, and trace IDs to correlate.
[02:45] Jorge Martinez: do we have a runbook we can read?
[02:48] Maya Patel: yes I'll share a short runbook after the call, includes playbook and rollback criteria.
[02:55] Aisha Khan: on triggers — is the policy only latency-based? we need error-rate triggers too, for hallucinations and NER failures.
[03:02] Liam O'Connor: good point. we can configure multi-metric policies: p95 latency, 5xx error rate, and a custom eval metric (factuality score). We recommend combined rule: if any two breach threshold for 2 consecutive windows, trigger.
[03:18] Lauren Green: sample thresholds?
[03:20] Liam O'Connor: p95 > 380ms, 5xx > 1%, factuality delta > 5 points against baseline eval set.
[03:30] Jorge Martinez: what's the rollback timeline — we need an approximate time to cutover in an emergency?
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: switch is near-instant for routing change, but client visible impact is cache-warmup — 2 to 6 minutes for p95 to stabilize depending on request mix.
[03:50] Samir Desai: ok that's acceptable. now on model pinning — do we pin by route or by customer? we want different customers to test different variants.
[04:00] Maya Patel: Redwood supports per-route and per-customer pinning. for this pilot we recommend per-route pinning: reconciliation routes pinned to radix-v1 for stability, chat pinned to radix-v1-q4, with a canary cohort of 5% of users hit with breeze-small for perf comparison.
[04:20] Aisha Khan: how do we rollback if the canary shows higher hallucination? is the A/B automatically paused?
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: yes we can auto-pause canaries if factuality metric drops below threshold. Also manual override via Console to force an emergency swap.
[04:35] Aisha Khan: there were a few transcription issues in the sample logs — sometimes 'KV' becomes 'K-B' in our logs, is that a concern?
[04:42] Liam O'Connor: that's just ASR in our test tooling, not the runtime logs; runtime logs use structured traces. We'll attach raw traces to the runbook.
[04:55] Maya Patel: ok moving on to measure plan — we need to collect p50/p95/p99, token cost per route, and per-request trace ids. Liam can you capture that in the post-run sheet?
[05:04] Liam O'Connor: yes will include per-route breakdown and heatmaps; also will add cache-warmup curve and cold-start latency percentiles.
[05:12] Jorge Martinez: any compliance flags before we run the dry-run? we couldn't get final SOC2 pack yet.
[05:18] Maya Patel: compliance review is scheduled next week — we won't do production cutovers before that's in. Dry-run is staging only.
[05:24] Lauren Green: good. about cost — do you have a rough per-million token delta for quantized vs full model?
[05:30] Liam O'Connor: rough numbers: radix-v1-q4 about 40% token-cost reduction vs radix-v1 in our staging profile. breeze-small about 65% reduction but bigger quality tradeoffs. We'll provide exact numbers by Tuesday.
[05:45] Aisha Khan: competitor question — we evaluated Bedrock earlier, they had good infra but less granular pinning. can Redwood do partial traffic pin at session-level?
[05:52] Maya Patel: yes session-level pinning is possible with our routing keys; we can make session sticky to a model variant for the session lifecycle.
[06:00] Samir Desai: any required infra changes on our side?
[06:03] Liam O'Connor: minimal: we need to allow staging IPs to access your test VPC for metrics scraping, and a small agent for end-to-end synthetic traffic. We'll share terraform snippets.
[06:16] Jorge Martinez: timing — when can the staging dry-run happen?
[06:18] Maya Patel: earliest Monday 2026-06-15 EOD for Redwood to prepare. HelixPay to confirm by 2026-06-13.
[06:25] Aisha Khan: can you also run a failover test that simulates a region outage?
[06:29] Liam O'Connor: yes we have a region-failover playbook, that'll be part of the extended dry-run if you want. It exercises automatic fallback to a secondary region with compatible model variants. Note: cross-region increases latency — we'll capture that.
[06:44] Lauren Green: security question — where do logs live during the pilot? retention?
[06:48] Maya Patel: for Dedicated and Private we can support customer-managed storage; for hosted we'll provide encrypted logs with configurable retention. We'll include KMS integration notes in the packet.
[06:58] Jorge Martinez: ok let's recap next steps 
[07:00] Maya Patel: recap: 1) Redwood runs staging rollback dry-run and shares artifacts; 2) Maya shares runbook, heatmap, and per-route cost; 3) HelixPay confirms success criteria; 4) schedule compliance deep-dive next week.
[07:12] Aisha Khan: and we'll validate the test harness and provide corner-case payloads.
[07:18] Maya Patel: perfect. any final questions?
[07:22] Lauren Green: none from me.
[07:24] Samir Desai: none.
[07:26] Jorge Martinez: thanks everyone.
[07:28] Maya Patel: thanks, we'll follow up in writing and post the runbook to the shared drive. Bye.
End of transcript.
